thread:
elaine: Pitch: "nightcap credits" idea. Offer customers an optional off-peak SLA with reduced reserved throughput (20-60%) during configurable local windows in exchange for a predictable credit on their monthly bill. Aimed at batch/offline workloads. Looking for product + ops sanity check.

mike: high level sounds useful. A few questions: recurring vs one-off windows? per-pool or per-tenant? how does this interact with Dedicated autoscale headroom?

elaine: MVP proposal: recurring per-pool windows, timezone-aware, multiple windows allowed. Autoscale remains but we cap headroom inside the nightcap window.

sara: Ops note: must include an automated safety abort if latency or error SLOs degrade. We need clear thresholds so pages don't spike. Also require a manual override in the Console.

jason: Commercial/legal: terms must state the credit math, pilot opt-out terms, and a fallback guarantee (route to hosted variant or allow burst billing at higher unit price). Launch criteria should include at least two paying pilots and a runbook signed off by SRE.

adrian: Implementation thought: admission layer stores nightcap policy objects with schedule and multiplier. While active, admission enforces a lower token rate and emits a RuntimeHint to reduce batch-size and cache retention. Telemetry: measure actual tokens admitted vs expected and p50/p95 latency deltas.

hana: Sales: Acme and Beacon AI both expressed interest in something like this. Beacon wants nightly embeddings cheaper; they asked for per-window credits applied pro-rata to invoices.

mike: runtime concerns: reducing throughput can increase KV churn and tail latency. We should allow a "cache_preserve" hint on the policy so runtime prioritizes hot keys during windows. Also we need to simulate steady-state tail impact before pilot.

sara: safety triggers proposal: p95 latency > 1.8x SLO for 3m -> auto-abort; error-rate increase > 4 percentage points for 5m -> auto-abort + page; manual abort in Console with one-click revert. Add a cooldown so we don't flip repeatedly.

jason: UI/API: Console calendar view, preview of monthly credit impact, audit trail. API endpoint example: POST /api/v1/reserved_pools/{id}/nightcap_windows. Include recurrence rule, multiplier, discount_pct, timezone, and safety thresholds.

elaine: sample API payload (informal):

"""
POST /api/v1/reserved_pools/789/nightcap_windows
{
  "rrule": "FREQ=DAILY",
  "start_time": "23:00",
  "end_time": "04:00",
  "multiplier": 0.5,
  "discount_pct": 30,
  "timezone": "Europe/London",
  "safety": {"p95_ms": 1500, "error_pct": 5}
}
"""

mike: good. For billing, pro-rata per-window credit is the simplest. Ensure invoices show a line-item for nightcap credits and a reconciliation view in the Console.

hana: customers asked for an upfront estimator: if you pick X windows and Y multiplier, here's estimated monthly credit. We should include that in the Console before opting in.

adrian: engineering estimate: admission/controller and runtime hints => 3 sprints; Console UI + estimator => 2 sprints; billing + invoice UI => 1 sprint; runbook + canary => 1 sprint. That's optimistic but doable if prioritized.

sara: add to checklist: oncall drill, synthetic load test during window, telemetry dashboards for delta vs baseline, and documented rollback steps.

jason: pilot criteria: two customers in different regions/timezones, 14-day internal canary, 7-day customer pilot, SLA escape validated twice in drills.

elaine: decision items: pricing ladder (flat pct vs multiplier tiers), cooldown/backoff policy after auto-abort, conflict resolution with other pool policies (preemption, soft-spill). Propose: conflicts resolved by priority: safety > emergency operator > preemption > nightcap. Nightcap is revocable.

adrian: also need admission-level metrics for billing usage vs expected to avoid disputes. Emit per-window admitted tokens and a window attribution tag.

hana: commercial ask: allow customers to apply nightcap only to a subset of models in a reserved pool (e.g., non-critical model IDs). That reduces risk. We should support model selectors in policy.

sara: ops: that's more complex but safer. Include as pilot v2. Pilot v1 scope: pool-level only. Pilot v2: model selectors.

elaine: action items: @adrian draft RFC for policy model and telemetry tags; @mike run cache/tail simulations and share expected deltas; @jason prepare pilot contract template and invoicing lines; @sara write runbook + drill plan; @hana line up pilot customers. ops-bot, please create tickets.

ops-bot: Created tickets IRIS-99901 (RFC: nightcap policy), IRIS-99902 (Console: nightcap UI + estimator), IRIS-99903 (Billing: nightcap credits), IRIS-99904 (Runbook + oncall drills).

elaine: Thanks all. I'll take the sales sync and circle back next Wed with prioritized timeline. If anyone objects to priority, speak now. :thumbsup:
